text.p: Israel's B.V.R. Technologies Ltd said on Thursday it won a $2.8 million contract from a European member of NATO for the supply of the Ehud rangeless real-time and post-flight debriefing system.
The contract is worth $2.8 million with additional options to be ordered within a month worth $400,000 to $800,000.
Delivery of the system, to be used on F-16 fighters, is expected before the end of 1997.
The contract is an initial purchase with follow-up orders expected within one to two years.
The country is the sixth to order the Ehud for its air force.

Ehud consists of airborne pods housed in training air-to-air missile shells adaptable to any type of combat aircraft. It provides real-time missile hit/miss simulation and assessment; midair and ground collision avoidance warnings; and post-flight debriefing.
